name: Saint Augustine Zhao Rong and Companions
history: One hundred and twenty martyrs who died in China over nearly three centuries: eighty-seven Chinese Catholics, priests, catechists, laymen, women and children, and thirty-three missionaries from Europe. Augustine Zhao Rong, a soldier who became a priest, died in prison in 1815. Saint John Paul II canonised them together in 2000.
life: Christianity reached China more than once, and from the seventeenth century missionaries built communities that endured repeated persecution. The first of these martyrs, the Dominican Francis Fernández de Capillas, was killed in 1648. Augustine Zhao Rong was a soldier who escorted the French missionary bishop Gabriel Taurin Dufresse to his martyrdom in 1815. Moved by the bishop’s patience, he asked for baptism, was ordained priest, and was himself arrested, tortured and died in prison. Many of the others died in the violence of 1900, among them whole families, catechists, seminarians, and girls in their teens, some of whom were offered their lives if they would renounce Christ and refused. The last died in 1930. The Church honours them not for any cause of nation or politics but because they would not deny Christ, and many died praying for those who killed them.
prayerTo: Holy martyrs of China, you were soldiers and farmers, priests and children, and you would not deny Christ. Pray for the Catholics of China and for all their people, that the Gospel may be heard there in freedom. Pray for me, that I may love Christ more than my life. Amen.
penance: Pray a decade of the Rosary today for the Church in China, and offer a small fast, perhaps a simple meal, for persecuted Christians everywhere.
meditation: A soldier watched a bishop die and asked to be baptised. Who is watching how you carry your cross?
